name: sticky-grid-scroll
title: Sticky Grid Scroll
description: A scroll-driven image grid in a sticky section: columns slide in from above and below, the grid zooms open, and a title, description and action settle into the space.
label: Theo Plawinski sticky grid scroll
author: Theo Plawinski <https://github.com/theoplawinski>
attribution: Copyright (c) 2025 Theo Plawinski; copyright (c) 2009 - 2025 Codrops. MIT License.

props.name: images
props.description: The grid's images, distributed over the columns in order (twelve in the original layout). An empty alt marks one decorative.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading: it fades in as the section arrives, then rises when the grid has opened.

props.name: description
props.description: Shown under the title once the grid has opened.

props.name: action
props.description: A link or button under the description, for example See the work; not focusable until it is shown.

props.name: columns
props.description: Columns in the grid. Even columns arrive from above, odd ones from below; the outer columns move out and the middle one splits as it zooms.

props.name: container
props.description: The element that scrolls, when it is not the window. Give it container-type: size so the section's heights follow it.

props.name: parallax
props.description: Slide the section up from under the content above it as it enters (put a positioned block with z-index 1 above it).

a11y: A section with a real heading (h2 by default); the images keep their alt text, and an empty alt marks one decorative.
The description and action stay out of the accessibility tree and the tab order (inert) until they are shown, and come back when the grid opens.
Under prefers-reduced-motion nothing moves with scroll: the section is one screen tall and shows the opened grid with the title, description and action in place.
Scrolling stays native (the keyboard, find in page and assistive technology work); the effect only follows the scroll position.
Colors are prefixed tokens (--sticky-grid-scroll-surface, --sticky-grid-scroll-foreground), black on white by default, with a dark pair; under prefers-contrast: more the action is underlined.
